paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it. God opens with a question so simple it almost sounds silly: "Do men fall and not get up again? Does one turn away and not return?" (Jeremiah 8:4). Of course you get back up. Of course you turn around. But God says His people "refuse to return" (Jeremiah 8:5), and not one of them stops to ask, "What have I done?" (Jeremiah 8:6).

Falling is human, but this was far more than a stumble, because God names greed and deceit running from the least of them to the greatest (Jeremiah 8:10). They dressed the wound with very little care and said "Peace, peace," when there was "no peace at all" (Jeremiah 8:11). That's what a hard heart does, baker: it swaps honest repair for a nice-sounding word. Even the birds keep their seasons, but God's people did not know the requirements of the LORD (Jeremiah 8:7).

So what do you do with this? You let the question "What have I done?" be a door and not a threat. When you catch yourself off course, you stop, you tell the truth, and you turn back to the Lord and His word. I tried to hide my own blurry edges for years, and it never fixed one cookie. Coming back to Him is how you finally get back up.
